 Wales vs Portugal predictions: Visitors confirmed as group winners

 Wales Portugal UEFA Nations League A Wales vs Portugal Our betting expert shares the best Wales vs Portugal predictions & tips, with the visitors needing only a point to win Group A4 in the Nations League.
 Wales need to adopt a more attacking approach and put Portugal under pressure. An open game could play into the visitors’ hands.

 Inexperienced Welsh forward line to draw a blank
 Wales have had a torrid Nations League campaign in the last couple of months. Craig Bellamy’s men sit at the foot of their group and have managed just three goals scored in five matches. They drew a blank in their trip to Portugal earlier in the group stage.
 Their underlying numbers offer little encouragement, either. Wales have recorded the second-lowest xG in League A at 3.7, suggesting their lack of goals is not simply down to poor finishing. They register an average of just 3.2 shots on target per game and have created just eight big chances in five matches.
 Bellamy has put his faith in youngster Lewis Koumas to impress in the final third. The Liverpool prospect has an average of just 6.13 in his five appearances.
 Portugal haven’t kept clean sheets in four of their last five, but we can see them shutting the Welsh out for a second game in a row. We can back a clean sheet for Portugal at a 51.28% implied probability. This looks like the top value play from our trio of Wales vs Portugal predictions.
 Wales vs Portugal Bet 1: Both teams to score (no) at odds of 1.95 with BET99 
 Portuguese to win by at least a two-goal margin
 Portugal have lost only one of their last nine away games in all competitions. They won by a two-goal margin at Parken in Copenhagen against Denmark last month. The Danes are a much better, more experienced outfit than Wales at present.
 With the hosts likely to push players forward in search of goals, Portugal should have opportunities to exploit the spaces left behind. Portugal average two goals scored per game in this competition.
 If Wales fail to get on the scoresheet, an away win by at least a two-goal margin looks realistic here. Portugal’s xG is the sixth best in League A (8.2). They also average the second-most shots on target per match (6.8). We can back this outcome at a modest 46.51% implied probability.
 Wales vs Portugal Bet 2: Portugal -1 (Handicap 3-way) at odds of 2.15 with BET99 
 Félix to fire Portugal to victory
 João Félix is the joint top scorer for Portugal in the 2026-27 Nations League, with three goals to his name. He has four goal contributions in total across his five appearances in League A.
 Félix has been in stunning form in the Saudi Pro League. He has nine goal contributions in his last four Saudi Pro League appearances for Al Nassr. He has also earned a rating of at least 9.0 in three of those matches.
 With lots of flashes of brilliance in recent weeks, the 27-year-old will be eager to exploit any gaps left by the Welsh defence. Félix’s goals per 90 record in the Nations League puts him in the 77th percentile. We can back him to score anytime at a 48.78% implied probability.
 Wales vs Portugal Bet 3: João Félix anytime goalscorer at odds of 2.05 with BET99 
 Our analysis: Form of both teams
 Score prediction: Wales 0-2 Portugal
 Goalscorers prediction: Portugal: Félix, Fernandes
 Wales host Portugal in Cardiff on Tuesday at 2:45pm ET needing a miracle to clinch a relegation play-off place. They are three points behind third-placed Norway, with a poorer goal difference by five goals.
 Craig Bellamy’s side lost 3-1 in Oslo on Saturday. Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland all scored for Norway. David Brooks replied for the Welsh as a second-half substitute. Wales sit bottom of Group A4 on three points.
 Portugal arrive on 12 points, having already reached the quarter-finals. They were beaten 4-1 by Denmark in Braga.
 Jorge Jesus still needs a point for his team to top the group. This is also the first squad selected since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football.
 Nuno Mendes is set to miss out through injury, and Ruben Dias is also banned after accumulating enough yellow cards to serve a ban. Joao Cancelo returns after serving a ban of his own against Denmark.
 Gustavo Varela earns a maiden call-up as Serie A’s leading scorer. Wales beat Norway 2-1 in Cardiff last month for their only win. They often enjoy playing in front of their own fans, with the Cardiff City Stadium well-known for its patriotic atmosphere.
 Probable lineups for Wales vs Portugal
 Wales expected lineup: Darlow, Dasilva, Roberts, Rodon, Davies, Johnson, James, Colwill, Cullen, Wilson, Koumas
 Portugal expected lineup: D. Costa, Cancelo, Dalot, A. Silva, Veiga, Neto, Vitinha, Neves, Felix, Fernandes, Ramos
